title: Quiz engine and UI with seed question bank

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 1, audited commit a03a9c5 (code identical to fe1aca0; a03a9c5 only fills in the approvals section of the sprint file). The sprint file was re-read fresh before this verdict.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. One confirmed requirement defect (R3/AC3). Everything else meets its criterion.

REQUIRED FIX (blocking):
1. R3 duplicate-id check ignores the "Comparisons ignore case and leading/trailing whitespace" rule. site/js/validate.js keys firstIndexOfId on the raw entry.id, so R3's rule is applied to 2 of its 3 listed comparisons (distractor vs correctAnswer, duplicate choices) and not to the third (duplicate id). README narrowed the rule to match ("Comparisons for 'same answer' ignore case..."), which is not what R3 says. Repro, run from repo root against validateQuestions:
   ["order-001","ORDER-001"]   -> 0 problems   (should be 1: duplicate id)
   ["order-001"," order-001 "] -> 0 problems   (should be 1: duplicate id)
   ["order-001","order-001"]   -> 1 problem    (correct)
   The CLI (npm run validate) calls the same function, so the automated check lets both through. Fix: key the duplicate map on normalize(entry.id) and report the original id in the message. Add tests for the case-variant and whitespace-variant duplicate ids that assert the message names the id. Correct the README sentence to state the rule as R3 does. This is a code-only change: site/data/questions.json must NOT change, so the R14 approval at fe1aca0 stays valid. If the data file changes, it needs product-owner re-approval.

CRITERIA, checked:
AC1 Met. README documents the Actions workflow and the exact setting (Pages source: GitHub Actions). No root-absolute URLs in site/. Assets are relative, the data URL is resolved from import.meta.url, and the favicon is inline so there is no /favicon.ico 404.
AC2 Met. site/data/questions.json is separate from the code. The validator enforces exactly the R2 fields (missing and extra fields are both flagged), their types, the four categories, 3 distractors, and a one-line fact.
AC3 NOT MET, see fix 1. Otherwise good: every other R3 violation is tested and the tests assert that the message names the id, including through the CLI's stderr and not just its exit code.
AC4 Met, mechanically. 12 entries, 3 per category, no current/most-recent phrasing, and order-003 uses 22nd and 24th. No Trump question. Historical accuracy is NOT certified by QA1; that is R14's job.
AC5 Met. Skewed-bank tests (30/2/2/2 and 40/1/1/1). The test proves the naive draw fails over 10% of the time, so the rule is actually being exercised. The engine enforces the rule itself and fails loudly if the invariant is broken.
AC6 Met. Over 500 rounds the correct answer lands in all 4 slots, each at 20-30% share. Each question's choice order also varies between showings.
AC7 Met. The handler disables every choice before calling session.answer(). answer() sets the lock before touching the score and returns null for any later call. Tests cover double-click, switched answers, and a same-tick burst. There is no double-fire path.
AC8 Met. The copy matches exactly. The em dash is U+2014, confirmed from the file bytes (E2 80 94), and the full stop is present. Marking uses tag text (a check or cross plus the words), a dashed vs solid border, and colour.
AC9 Met. Screens and labels are exact. Play again builds a new QuizSession, so the score resets with no page reload (grep finds no reload anywhere). Next is hidden until an answer is given, and nothing is timed.
AC10 Met. No fixed widths, overflow-wrap is anywhere, choices are width 100%, and .btn has a 44px minimum.
AC11 Met. Choices are real buttons and the feedback is in role=status aria-live=polite. Focus goes to the question heading after Next and on the first question, to Next after an answer, and to the results heading at the end. The focus ring is visible.
AC12 Met. QA1 ran npm test on Node 24.21.0: 54/54 pass. npm run validate: OK on 12 questions.
AC13 Met. No storage, cookie, beacon, analytics, or external request anywhere in site/. The only URL is the SVG namespace string in the inline icon.
AC14 Met. The approvals section records fe1aca0 and quotes the product owner's "Approved". git diff fe1aca0 a03a9c5 -- site/data/questions.json is empty.

ADVISORY (non-blocking, not required for PASS):
a. Live-region timing: feedback-text is set while #feedback is display:none and the region is un-hidden in the same tick. Some screen reader and browser combinations do not announce a region that enters the accessibility tree already filled. Suggest keeping the region always rendered and toggling only its content. Worth a real check by LiveQA or sprint 3's a11y audit.
b. main.js validates the bank's shape but not whether it covers at least 3 categories. A bank that is valid but covers too few categories would make drawRound throw inside the Start click handler. That exception is uncaught and the student sees nothing. This can't happen with the current data. Consider checking it in loadBank so it reaches the #load-error path.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, round 2, sprint 1. Audited commit be87be8. The working tree was clean.

VERDICT: PASS.

SPRINT FILE: re-checked. git diff a03a9c5 be87be8 on the sprint file is empty, so the requirements are unchanged since round 1's fresh read.

ROUND-1 FIX (R3/AC3): FIXED. site/js/validate.js now keys the duplicate-id map on normalize(id), the same rule the other two R3 comparisons use, and the message still names the offending id. QA1 re-ran the round-1 repro against validateQuestions:
  ["order-001","ORDER-001"]   -> 1 problem (duplicate id), names "ORDER-001"
  ["order-001"," order-001 "] -> 1 problem (duplicate id), names " order-001 "
  ["order-001","order-001"]   -> 1 problem
  ["order-001","order-002"]   -> 0 problems (no over-matching)
Four new tests cover the case variant, the whitespace variant, distinct ids, and the CLI's stderr and exit code for a case variant. The README now states R3's rule as written.

AC12: QA1 ran npm test: 58/58 pass. npm run validate: OK on 12 questions.

AC14: still met. git diff fe1aca0 be87be8 on site/data/questions.json is empty, so the product-owner approval recorded at fe1aca0 covers the data under audit.

All other criteria (AC1, AC2, AC4-AC11, AC13) were met in round 1, and the round-2 diff (README.md, site/js/validate.js, tests/validate.test.mjs) touches none of them.

ADVISORY items a and b from round 1 (live-region timing, and an uncaught error if the bank covers too few categories) remain open and non-blocking. Recommend LiveQA or sprint 3 check (a) with a real screen reader.

commit=be87be8 | ci=undeterminable: could not run gh to query CI runs for be87be84cb569e72fd21592304af80d1fe4db81a ([WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified) — gh may not be installed, or the query timed out.

PASS: LiveQA live test, sprint 1, round 1. Deployed commit tested: be87be84cb569e72fd21592304af80d1fe4db81a.
Environment: https://arjansahota02-bit.github.io/Test/ on 2026-09-19. Desktop Chrome, driven through the Claude in Chrome extension, viewport 1920x911, DPR 1. The 320px round used a 320 CSS px same-origin iframe of the live URL (EMULATION, not a phone). The double-tap check used the product owner's real phone (device and browser not stated).

VERDICT: PASS. All five live-test criteria were verified. No product defects were found.

DEPLOY IDENTITY: curl fetched the deployed index.html, styles.css, js/main.js, js/app.js, js/quiz.js, js/validate.js and data/questions.json. All 7 are byte-identical (cmp) to site/ at be87be8. origin/main is 8f1718a, and git diff be87be8 8f1718a touches only docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json.

CRITERION 1, URL loads with no 404s: PASS. A reload with network tracking on made 7 requests, all 200 and all same-origin: /Test/, styles.css, js/main.js, js/app.js, js/validate.js, js/quiz.js, data/questions.json. The console had no messages. No /favicon.ico is requested; the icon link is a data:image/svg+xml URL. document.cookie was empty, and localStorage.length and sessionStorage.length were both 0 (R13). This confirms R1's /Test/ subpath assumption on the real host.

CRITERION 2, full round with right and wrong answers, exact copy, score, Play again: PASS. Mouse round (trusted clicks, capture-phase logger on): Q2 and Q3 were answered wrong on purpose and the other 8 right. The results screen showed "Your score 8 / 10 Play again", exactly as expected.
  Verbatim wrong: "Incorrect — the answer is John F. Kennedy. Kennedy delivered the line at his inauguration on January 20, 1961." The dash is U+2014 (checked by char code). The feedback icon was "✗".
  Verbatim right: "Correct! McKinley died on September 14, 1901, eight days after being shot, and Roosevelt was sworn in as president."
  Wrong-answer marking: my choice read "✗ Your answer — incorrect" with a dashed border, and the correct choice read "✓ Correct answer" with a solid border. The marking uses text as well as colour.
  All 10 questions' feedback text matched the deployed bank's fact field exactly.
  Play again: a window marker set before the round survived, and performance navigation entries stayed at 1, so there was no reload. It returned to "Question 1 of 10" with a different first question, and the next round's result (9 / 10) did not carry the previous 8.
  Next was hidden until an answer was given. Nothing advanced on its own.
  Round draws seen: 3 rounds, each with 10 unique ids and at least 3 categories (all 4 in the mouse and keyboard rounds). Choice order varied between showings: Lincoln was in position 1, then 2; Theodore Roosevelt was in position 2, then 4.

CRITERION 3, rapid double-click and double-tap: PASS.
  Mouse double-click on the correct answer, then clicks on two other choices. Logged: a trusted pointerdown and click on "Theodore Roosevelt" at t=58510/58511, a second pointerdown at t=58514 on the same button already disabled:true (no second click fired), then pointerdowns on Chester A. Arthur and Theodore Roosevelt, both disabled:true. Exactly one answer was recorded. The final score matched the expected count in every round (8/10, 9/10, 6/10).
  Keyboard: 3 Enter presses on a choice produced one answer. Enter 2 activated Next, and Enter 3 hit the heading and did nothing. The score was unaffected (the final 9/10 matched).
  Real-device double-tap by the product owner, verbatim: "Only one answer got marked, i only could answer once and once I clicked a answer, it said that was my pick and then said if I was wrong or not".

CRITERION 4, keyboard-only round: PASS. It used Tab, Enter and Space only: 64 logged key events and zero pointer events. It ended at "Your score 9 / 10", exactly as expected (Q4 was wrong on purpose). Space activates a choice as well as Enter. Focus moved to the question heading after every Next (activeElement id question-heading), to Next after every answer, and to results-heading at the end. Tab then reached Play again, and Enter started a new round. Focus is visible: focused choice :focus-visible true, outline "solid 3px rgb(29, 78, 216)"; Next and Play again :focus-visible true.

CRITERION 5, 320px: PASS, on EMULATION (a 320 CSS px same-origin iframe, innerWidth 320). A full round was measured on 22 screens (start, each question before and after answering, results). Maximum documentElement.scrollWidth was 320, and no element's right edge went past 320. On the longest question (the Kennedy quote, with feedback shown) scrollWidth equalled clientWidth (305/305) once the vertical scrollbar appeared. The smallest visible button was 79x48 (Next), choices were 288x48 (288x74 when marked), and Start quiz was 114x48. The round scored "Your score 6 / 10", exactly as expected (6). Clicks in this round were synthetic .click() calls inside the frame, because this is a layout check. Real-device cross-browser is sprint 3's gate.

OBSERVATIONS (non-blocking, not spec violations):
a. Holding or hammering Enter skips the feedback. Focus moves to Next as soon as an answer is given, so a second Enter advances immediately. On Q1 of the keyboard round, 3 Enter presses answered and then left the question before the feedback could be read. R7 is met (the answer and score were unchanged). This is a UX question for Master Controller: should Next ignore activation for a short time, or should focus go somewhere else? It is not a defect against R7, R9 or R11 as written.
b. QA1 advisory (a), live-region announcement timing: NOT verified. No screen reader was available. The DOM matches QA1's description: #feedback has role=status, aria-live=polite, aria-atomic=true, and the hidden attribute is toggled. This is still for sprint 3's a11y audit.
c. Test-harness artifact, not a product defect: in my first, uninstrumented attempt the app recorded "Andrew Johnson" as my answer, which is not what I aimed at. Investigation: the tab was document.visibilityState "hidden" throughout. Screenshots stalled (CDP captureScreenshot timeouts), and on a controlled replay the tool reported 2 clicks as successful while the page's capture-phase logger received 0 events. The tool's input delivery in that attempt is unknown. In the instrumented rounds, all 20 trusted-input answers were recorded against exactly the element the logger showed was targeted.
d. resize_window to 320 had no effect (innerWidth stayed 1920), which is why the iframe was used.

Evidence screenshots (local): C:\Users\arjan\AppData\Local\Temp\claude-chrome-screenshots-9iEqB1\ screenshot-1789847418224-0.jpg (start screen), -1789847683196-3.jpg (Play again, fresh Q1), -1789847896226-4.jpg (320px, wrong answer marked, both marks, Next focused), -1789847493747-2.jpg (uninstrumented attempt, see c).
